question: What is the primary substance used as a contrast medium in a barium meal?
explanation: Barium sulfate is a dense metallic compound that coats the gut lining to absorb x-rays and create clear images. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h1)

question: Why does barium sulfate appear clearly on x-ray films?

options.A: It has a high atomic number
options.C: It dissolves completely in blood plasma
options.D: It reacts with stomach acid to produce gas

explanation: Elements with high atomic numbers absorb x-rays much better than soft tissues, creating high contrast on the radiograph. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h1)

question: A patient with difficulty swallowing is evaluated using a barium meal to check for what condition?
explanation: Dysphagia often points to narrowing or strictures in the esophagus, which a barium swallow clearly outlines. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h2)

question: A patient presents with recurrent upper abdominal pain and dark, tarry stools. Which diagnostic procedure is most appropriate to visualize mucosal lesions?
explanation: Dark tarry stools suggest upper GI bleeding, and a barium meal helps identify bleeding sources like gastric ulcers. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is the primary absolute contraindication for performing a barium meal?
explanation: Leaking barium outside the gastrointestinal tract into the peritoneal cavity causes severe chemical peritonitis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h3)

question: What complication can occur if barium is given to a patient with a severe bowel obstruction?

options.A: The patient develops sudden systemic infection
options.B: The barium hardens and worsens the blockage
options.C: The contrast dissolves and enters the bloodstream
options.D: The stomach wall stretches and ruptures instantly

explanation: Barium absorbs water as it travels through a blocked gut, solidifying into a hard mass that worsens the obstruction. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h3)

question: How long should a patient typically fast before undergoing a barium meal procedure?
explanation: An empty stomach is required so that leftover food particles do not hide ulcers or tumors during imaging. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why is a patient advised to avoid smoking on the morning of a barium meal?

options.A: Smoking causes immediate allergic reactions to barium
options.B: Smoking completely neutralizes the contrast medium
options.C: Nicotine makes the x-ray machine malfunction
options.D: Nicotine increases gastric acid secretion and motility

explanation: Nicotine stimulates the stomach to produce more acid and move faster, interfering with clear visualization. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the purpose of giving effervescent granules during a double-contrast barium meal?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of the contrast
options.B: To prevent the patient from vomiting barium
options.C: To produce gas for better mucosal coating
options.D: To numb the lining of the esophagus

explanation: Effervescent granules release gas, which pushes the barium against the stomach wall for a clearer double-contrast view. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why does the radiologist tilt the examination table into different positions during the procedure?

options.A: To reduce the amount of radiation exposure
options.B: To prevent the patient from falling asleep
options.C: To ensure the barium coats all mucosal surfaces
options.D: To help the patient empty their bladder faster

explanation: Changing body positions allows gravity to pull the liquid barium across every part of the stomach and duodenum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: What colour should the nurse inform the patient their stool will be after a barium meal?
explanation: The unabsorbed barium gives the stool a distinct pale, chalky appearance until it is completely eliminated. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why are increased fluids and laxatives routinely ordered after a barium meal examination?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing nausea
options.B: To dilute the remaining stomach acid safely
options.C: To prevent severe constipation and barium impaction
options.D: To speed up absorption of barium into the blood

explanation: Barium dries out inside the large intestine, so extra fluids and laxatives help push it out before it forms a blockage. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is the most frequent minor complication experienced by patients after a barium meal?
explanation: Barium tends to dry out in the lower bowel, making constipation the most common side effect following the test. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h7)

question: Which complication should the nurse monitor for if an elderly patient accidentally inhales barium during the swallow?
explanation: Inhaling barium into the respiratory tree causes inflammation and infection known as aspiration or chemical pneumonia. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h7)
